newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton settles weaker and below key level.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton settles weaker and below key level.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed weaker and below key 76.00 cents in May, suggesting further losses may be in store Friday, market sources said.
Producer selling and a dearth of buying interest was noted from the outset after what most players deemed a disappointing report from the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
The USDA said exports rose 37 percent in the week ended February 20 from the previous week, and 14 percent from the four-week average.
New sales were put at 243,000 480-lb bales and exports at 226,600 bales, for the 1996/97 marketing year.
But the market had anticipated exports of about 300,000 bales after the May contract hit a life-of-contract low of 73.00 cents, on February 18.

Many market sources expect the USDA to raise its export target from 6.5 million bales to about 6.8 million bales by the end of the season. Based on the weekly data, however, exports are in line to reach only the current estimate, Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said.
The May contract closed down 0.44 cent at 75.87 cents per pound, traded 76.00 to 75.60 cents. March settled 0.26 cent lower at 74.20 cents.
Volume was light at an estimated 6,000 lots, compared to Wednesday's official volume of 12,922 lots.
Nearby resistance was seen at 76.00 cents and then at 77.25 cents basis May.
